verified_facts.text: The hotel is at Fifth Avenue and 55th Street in Midtown Manhattan, steps from Central Park, Fifth Avenue shopping, MoMA and Rockefeller Center.

verified_facts.text: John Jacob Astor IV founded The St. Regis New York in 1904.
verified_facts.excerpt: In 1904, John Jacob Astor IV founded The St. Regis New York

verified_facts.text: The hotel was declared a New York City Landmark in 1988.

verified_facts.text: The King Cole Bar is the home of the original Bloody Mary.

verified_facts.text: In 1934 bartender Fernand Petiot introduced the Red Snapper, which was later renamed the Bloody Mary.

verified_facts.text: The name Bloody Mary was deemed too vulgar for the King Cole Bar, so the drink was rechristened the Red Snapper.

verified_facts.text: The Old King Cole mural was painted by Maxfield Parrish in 1906 for the Knickerbocker hotel on 42nd Street.
verified_facts.excerpt: The puckish mural, painted by Maxfield Parrish in 1906, was commissioned by Colonel John Jacob Astor for his 42nd Street hotel, The Knickerbocker.

verified_facts.text: The Maxfield Parrish mural arrived at The St. Regis New York in 1932.
verified_facts.excerpt: before arriving at its home in The St. Regis New York in 1932.

verified_facts.text: The Drawing Room, formerly Astor Court, is a lounge-style space next to the King Cole Bar serving sharable bites and large plates.
